newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Steady despite ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Steady despite ample supplies.

text.p: Despite ample supplies and softer crude, the fuel oil market held steady on Tuesday and traders said the upward momentum might continue in the near term.
The 180-cst grade was bid at $100 per tonne and offered at $101 for deliveries April 8-12 and April 2-12 respectively, traders said.
The return of one aggressive local trading company to the market on Monday boosted sentiment, but some traders were still searching for a confirmation for the uptrend.
"Prices seem pretty well supported," said one trader. "But in theory, prices should not be that firm because there are quite a lot of supplies."
Two local traders were heard to price up the market, buying two 20,000-tonne cargoes on Monday at $99.00 and $99.50 per tonne respectively for April lifting, traders said.
"If they really want to price up, they can buy as much as half a million tonnes in a month," said another trader.
Fuel oil swaps also edged higher slightly, with April last quoted at $99.50/$100.50 and May at $98.25/$99.50.

However, sentiment was cautious with most traders awaiting the next move of the local trading company which priced up the fuel oil market two weeks ago and has been on a buying spree in the gas oil market recently.
Traders noted that arbitrage cargoes from the Mediterranean to Asia could add pressure to the recent price rise.
European traders have estimated around 250,000 tonnes of fuel oil being worked from the Mediterranean for eastwards trips, mainly destined for Singapore, since early March.
In the LSWR market, demand remained poor as traders considered prices high.
